newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Camdessus says only discussed Russia 97 plans.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus says only discussed Russia 97 plans.

text.p: Russia and the IMF are talking about Moscow's economic plans for 1997-98, but IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday he had not discussed the payment of monthly tranches of a three-year loan.
"We have not discussed that yet with the authorities," Camdessus said, replying to a question about whether he would recommend payment of the monthly tranches.
Several tranches, worth around $340 million apiece, have been delayed because of IMF concern about low Russian tax revenues.

"What we have discussed so far is the 1997 programme for the country," Camdessus said. "We will possibly discuss (the monthly tranches) later on. We found it more important to focus on the big numbers."
Interfax news agency had said Camdessus was ready to recommend the release of the next $340 million tranche by the end of this month.
But Camdessus made clear at the news conference that he planned to recommend Russia's annual economic programme and that he had not been talking about individual monthly tranches.

"On the basis of the pledges the Russian authorities have been able to make, I have recommended to go ahead with the second tranche covering the end of this year and the beginning of next year," he said.
